modelAnswer:
Daniel and Rachel suggested that Emily continue her journey by train. A station in the next town still had trains running to Toronto, they explained. Emily hesitated. "But what about my car?" she asked. Daniel told her that a mechanic he knew could pull it out of the ditch once the snow stopped, and that it would be safe at his garage. Relieved, Emily thanked them again and again. That afternoon, the couple drove her to the station. Sitting by the train window, Emily watched the white fields slip past. On Christmas Eve, she stepped onto the platform in Toronto, where her boyfriend was waiting with open arms.

Three days later, Emily returned to get her car. Daniel and Rachel met her at the same little cafe, and this time she insisted on buying the hot chocolate. Together they went to the garage, where her car stood free of snow, already pulled out of the ditch. Emily paid the mechanic and handed the couple a box of cookies she had baked with her boyfriend on Christmas Day. "Without you, I would have spent Christmas alone in a ditch," she said. Rachel smiled and made her promise to check the weather next time. As Emily drove home slowly along the cleared highway, she realized that the storm had nearly ruined her holiday, but two strangers had turned it into one she would never forget.
